request: What did I spend at Amazon per month in 2025? The bookings just read AMZN Mktp DE.

plan.title: Amazon orders per month
plan.question: spending on the Amazon marketplace bookings (description starting with AMZN Mktp) per month of 2025, one row per month, ordered, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and total_eur

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
  AND lower(description) LIKE 'amzn mktp%'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
it follows one merchant over the months of a year, which is a trend
a line reads a trend most directly, and one merchant needs no series
the columns are month and total_eur, the euro column last
the period is 2025, the year the bookings cover
reasoning_code:
the shape is line, so the mark is lineY over the rows
the columns are month and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
months on x with monthShort, euros on y
a line brings no baseline of its own, so its euro axis names the domain over the amounts, zero included

request: How did my spending add up over 2025?

plan.title: Spending so far this year
plan.question: the running total of spending per month over 2025, one row per month with the cumulative figure, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and cumulative_eur

sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, SUM(-amount) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM months
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
'add up' is a running total over the months
an area under the running line reads the pace of it
the columns are month and cumulative_eur
the period is the whole of 2025
reasoning_code:
the shape is area, so areaY draws the band and lineY its edge
the columns are month and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
months on x with monthShort, euros on y
an area rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory

plan.question: spending of August 2025 and of December 2025 per category, one row per category and month, the month named 'August' or 'December', the five largest categories by total over both months, columns topic, period and total_eur
